newsitem.title: INDIA: India Maruti says post-tax profit 5.01 bln rupees.
newsitem.headline: India Maruti says post-tax profit 5.01 bln rupees.

text.p: India's Maruti Udyog Ltd on Monday said profit after tax for the financial year 1996/97 ending March 31 rose to 5.01 billion rupees ($139.56 million) from 4.28 billion in the previous year.
Maruti, a 50-50 joint venture between the Indian government and Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp, is India's largest carmaker.
It said 1996/97 post-tax earnings per share (EPS) rose to 378 rupees from 323 rupees in the previous financial year.
A company statement said its sales of vehicles rose to 338,690 in 1996/97 from 275,411 in the previous financial year.

"Maruti is already running at 134 percent of capacity and no new capacity would be added during 1997/98," the statement said. "For this reason production would increase marginally (to) 340,000 vehicles, (with) a small increase in exports to 38,000 vehicles is planned," it said.
It said exports in 1996/97 totalled 35,162 vehicles compared with 26,103 in the previous year. ($1 = 35.90 rupees)
